sections.html:
Resort city, Horry County, northeast corner of the state: that sums up Myrtle Beach, which sits at the center of the 60-mile Grand Strand. The Intracoastal Waterway has separated it from the mainland since 1936. With a median age near 50, many owners are retirees or second-home holders, and that shapes who sells and why.

City measureMyrtle Beach
Total area23.69 square miles, of which 23.42 is land
Population, 202035,682
Population, July 1, 2025 estimate40,937
Median age, 202049.4
IncorporatedTown in 1938, city in 1957
Public school districtHorry County Schools

Visitors fuel the economy, and they create a large pool of short-stay housing next to year-round homes. A house near a tourist corridor may earn more as a rental. One on a quiet residential street plays by different rules, covered next.

Under city rules, a rental of under 90 days is a short-term rental, and it is legal only where the zone permits it. Most traditional residential neighborhoods do not. Zone names beginning with R are shut out, with one exception, RMV (Residential Multifamily Visitor). The points below can affect a sale:

  • Renting a property requires a business license.
  • Fewer than 30 houses in traditional residential zones are exempt because they were used as short-term rentals before the current zoning.
  • A property outside a permitted zone cannot be converted to that use or approved for it.
  • A violation of the zoning code or business license ordinance is a misdemeanor, with fines of up to $500, 30 days, or both.

If someone has rented your house by the night, confirm its zone with the city Zoning Division at 843-918-1179 before you tell a buyer the rental can continue. A cash buyer will ask the same question, because the answer changes what the house is worth.

Hurricane Hazel in 1954 was the worst storm in the city's history, and Hugo in 1989 was the last hurricane to cause significant damage. Horry County took about $944 million in damage from Hugo, and beach erosion was severe in Myrtle Beach and North Myrtle Beach.

Buyers and their insurers still ask about roof age, wind-rated windows and flood coverage, so have those answers ready.

Oceanfront and golf-course areas draw different buyers than inland streets. A seller in Carver or Pine Lakes will see different comparable sales than one in Grande Dunes, so ask for sold prices from your own neighborhood and not the whole city.

Myrtle Beach International Airport is county-owned and about 3 miles southwest of downtown. U.S. 17, the U.S. 17 Bypass, U.S. 501, SC 31 and SC 73 (Ocean Boulevard) are the main roads.

Horry County does the assessing and billing for Myrtle Beach. Your legal residence is assessed at 4 percent of fair market value; everything else, including a second home or rental, at 6 percent. The bill is market value times that ratio times the millage rate. For 2023 the combined county, school, fire and waste rate was 216.2 mills, before any municipal charges.

Pay by January 15 to dodge penalties. After that come 3 percent, then 7 percent, then 5 percent. Questions go to the Auditor at 843-915-5051.

A few rules from the Assessor's guide are worth knowing before you sell:

  • Horry reassesses every four years, with the change taking effect in the fifth. The latest valuation date was December 31, 2023.
  • In the year a sale first becomes taxable, the 15 percent cap on increases does not protect the new owner.
  • An appeal must be in writing within 90 days of the reassessment notice. Go to the Assessor at 1301 2nd Avenue in Conway or call 843-915-5040.
  • After a move, the new house needs its own legal residence application. Tell the Assessor about a change of use within six months.

sections.h2: Recording a deed in Horry County
sections.html:
Go to the Horry County Register of Deeds, 1301 Second Avenue, Conway. Weekday hours are 8 a.m. to 4:45 p.m., and the number is (843) 915-5430.

Since August 1, 2019, recording most documents costs a flat fee instead of a per-page rate. The county's website carries the fee schedule. A separate transfer fee applies to the deed: $1.85 for every $500 of value, with $1.30 for the state and $0.55 for the county. File a value affidavit alongside it.

South Carolina requires owners to hand a buyer a written property condition statement unless the transfer is exempt, and the law allows as-is agreements. The text is in Title 27, Chapter 50. A house that was rented hard may carry wear a buyer's inspector will find, so decide ahead of time whether to fix, price around it or sell as it stands.

sections.h2: Selling a house that was a rental
sections.html:
Former short-term rentals often show heavy wear: tired furniture, worn flooring, appliances that were never meant for year-round use. A buyer who needs a loan will see those items on the inspection report and may ask for credits or walk away.

A cash buyer prices the condition in from the start. Before you list or call anyone, sort out three things: which zone the property is in, whether a business license was ever held and whether any code violation is open. Rental history that was lawful is easy to explain. History that was not can complicate any sale, so face it early and with the facts in hand.

sections.h2: Is a cash sale right for your house?
sections.html:
Consider one when the house needs work, took a beating as a rental or sits with heirs who live elsewhere. Cash Home Buyers looks at Myrtle Beach homes in their present condition and writes up any offer, which you can compare with listing on your own timetable.

The path is short. You describe the property, we look it over and, if an offer comes, you read it in writing. When you agree, you choose a closing date. A closing attorney or title company handles the paperwork, pays off a mortgage or tax balance from your proceeds and records the deed in Conway. Nobody orders an appraisal because no lender is involved.

Gather a few papers first: your latest tax bill, a payoff figure for any loan, the business license if the house was rented and, for inherited property, the estate documents. Also ask the county whether any tax balance is outstanding, since that comes out of proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: Is Myrtle Beach in Horry County?
faqs.a: Yes. Myrtle Beach is in Horry County, and the county assessor, auditor, treasurer and Register of Deeds all handle its property records.

faqs.q: Are short-term rentals allowed in every Myrtle Beach neighborhood?
faqs.a: No. The city says most traditional residential zones do not allow rentals under 90 days, and any zone starting with R is excluded except RMV. A business license is also required.

faqs.q: What is the deed transfer fee in South Carolina?
faqs.a: The fee is $1.85 per $500 of value or fraction, of which $1.30 goes to the state and $0.55 to the county. Estate distribution deeds and a few other transfers are exempt.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal my Horry County assessment?
faqs.a: Ninety days is the window, counted from the reassessment notice, and the appeal has to be in writing.

faqs.q: Does selling change my Myrtle Beach property tax?
faqs.a: For the buyer it can. The sale is an assessable transfer, which lifts the 15 percent cap in the first taxable year. The Assessor at 843-915-5040 can explain how it applies to your parcel.
